title: The Merchant and the Desert Robbers
summary: An honest spice merchant of Damascus was crossing the Syrian desert alone on his camel, carrying three bags of fragrant saffron and a leather pouch of two hundred gold dinars se...
full_text:
An honest spice merchant of Damascus was crossing the Syrian desert alone on his camel, carrying three bags of fragrant saffron and a leather pouch of two hundred gold dinars sewn inside four loaves of dry flatbread.

In a rocky ravine, twelve armed desert brigands rode down from the hills, surrounded his camel with leveled lances, and ordered him to dismount.

The merchant did not tremble or plead for mercy. He dismounted with calm dignity, unrolled his prayer mat upon the sand, and bowed respectfully to the robber chief:

'Welcome, travelers of the desert! The sun is sinking, and it is unseemly that men of the desert should meet without breaking bread. I have traveled far, and my only food is this water and four fresh loaves of bread. Sit with me by the rocks, and let us share my meal before you take my goods.'

The robber chief, surprised by his fearless courtesy, sat cross-legged with his men.

The merchant broke the four loaves of bread to distribute the pieces. As he did so, the seam opened, and the two hundred gold dinars spilled out onto the sand before the eyes of all twelve brigands!

The merchant looked at the gold, and then at the chief with an open smile: 'Take the gold if you will, brothers; it was earned by sweat, but hospitality is sacred. Eat the bread first, for food shared between men is a covenant of peace.'

The robber chief looked at the bread, and then at the merchant’s noble countenance. He was struck with profound shame.

'By heavens!' cried the chief, standing up. 'Shall we rob a man who invites his robbers to break bread, and whose hands are pure as spring water? Keep your gold, merchant, and keep your saffron!'

The twelve brigands not only refused to take a single coin, but escorted the merchant safely across the dangerous desert passes to Damascus, proving that sacred hospitality disarms the fiercest blades.
moral: Generous hospitality and courageous honesty disarm the fiercest outlaws.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Merchant and the Robbers"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
